name: Bradley Vision
caption: An opening-card wrestler on the promotion's debut show, released from the roster after being eliminated first from its opening battle royal.

tenures.note: Dropped the debut show's opener to Steve Greedy, then was eliminated first from the battle royal that crowned the first NEWC Television Champion; released from the roster shortly after, per the federation's own fourth bulletin.

name: Misery
caption: A wrestler who went undefeated through the promotion's first two shows before falling short of the NEWC Television Championship in its crowning battle royal.

identity.note: A common ring name shared with four unrelated held wrestlers at other wings; no operator, roster, title or URL ties this billing to any of them. Recorded distinct by default.

tenures.note: Undefeated through the debut show and second show, then eliminated second-to-last from the battle royal that crowned the first NEWC Television Champion; eliminated Chris Capri from a three-way dance on the third show before losing the fall to Alexander Anderson.

name: Nefarious
caption: A debut-show wrestler managed by a ringside second, who lost his own opening match.

tenures.note: Lost to Misery on the debut show; not mentioned again in the held record's surviving bulletins.

name: Takisuma Ogama
caption: A debut-show wrestler who won his opening match before losing the same night to Ethan Everitt.

identity.note: The same name places #136 tagged MLW in a 2001 RSPWF Top 200 edition. No roster, title, operator or date evidence ties that placing to this 2004 federation; recorded distinct by default.

tenures.note: Beat Neige Thirteen, then lost the same night to Ethan Everitt; not mentioned again in the held record's surviving bulletins.

name: Neige Thirteen
caption: A wrestler managed by a ringside second, winless through the promotion's first three shows and the target of a backstage attack on the third.

tenures.note: Lost on all three shows this collection preserves, the last by disqualification after a backstage attacker (billed as signed to the roster under a separate bulletin item) interfered.

name: Ethan Everitt
caption: Billed as the promotion's booker's own personal enforcer, undefeated on the debut show before dropping his next two outings.

tenures.note: Beat Takisuma Ogama on the debut show, billed as following orders from Commissioner Dave Powers alone; lost his next two matches, the second a battle royal elimination.

name: Alexander Anderson
caption: An undefeated wrestler through the promotion's first three shows, becoming the first man to qualify for its still-vacant Heavyweight Championship match.

tenures.note: Won all three of his matches across the promotion's first three shows, the third a three-way dance over Misery and Chris Capri that made him the first man to qualify for the NEWC Heavyweight Championship match.

name: "The Jackal" Bryan Vincent

identity.note: The bare name "Bryan Vincent" places #135 tagged SSGC in the 2003 RSPWF Top 200. No roster, title, operator or date evidence ties that placing to this 2004 federation; recorded distinct by default.

caption: One half of a running feud with Zack Sharp carried across the promotion's first two shows.

tenures.note: Debuted in a confrontation with Zack Sharp on the debut show; beat Sharp in a singles grudge match on the second show, then was eliminated from that same show's title battle royal.

name: "Sick & Twisted" Zack Sharp

identity.note: The bare name "Zack Sharp" already carries two unrelated held records from a different era and federation (1997 INWI, 1997 NWA), and a further "Technician" Zack Sharp RSPWF Top 200 placing under a different nickname. No axis ties any of them to this 2004 federation; recorded distinct by default.

caption: One half of a running feud with Bryan Vincent, later winning the promotion's own tag-team-scale grudge matches on his own.

tenures.note: Debuted in a confrontation with Bryan Vincent, losing their singles grudge match on the second show but eliminating him from that same show's title battle royal (before eliminating himself); beat Chris Preston on the third show.

name: Jeremiah Phoenix
caption: A late roster addition who reached the final of the promotion's first Television Championship battle royal.

tenures.note: First appearance on the roster; the runner-up in the ten-man battle royal that crowned the first NEWC Television Champion, pinned by Sabbath.

name: Dilli Ram Iyayi
caption: A previously unbilled attacker of Neige Thirteen who won his own first credited match by disqualification.

tenures.note: Credited only in the third show's Card Results section (absent from that bulletin's own numbered roster) as the attacker of Neige Thirteen, beating him by disqualification; billed "The Buddhist Monk" for the first time in the same bulletin's own next-show preview.

name: Alexey Isakova
caption: A debuting wrestler billed as "the pride of Belarus," winning his first match against a much larger opponent.

tenures.note: Debut win over The Strangler, billed as giving up roughly 60 pounds to his opponent.

name: The Strangler

identity.note: A different held wrestler also carries "The Strangler" as an aka, a decade-plus later at a different, unrelated wing (CAWO, 2016). No axis ties the two; recorded distinct by default.

caption: A debuting wrestler billed only as "a very mysterious man," who lost his first match to a much smaller opponent.

tenures.note: Debut loss to Alexey Isakova, billed as outweighing his opponent by roughly 60 pounds.

name: "Lowlife" Chris Preston
caption: A debuting wrestler with a ringside entourage of two, losing his first match to Zack Sharp.

tenures.note: Announced on the third bulletin's own roster, then lost his debut match to Zack Sharp on the third show.
